Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Symphony Health discovery + bakeoff plan

Hi Jenna / Todd — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations before the bakeoff.

High-level pain points you shared
- Response latency and cost are spiking when the inference workload shifts to longer contextual histories (clinical notes + prior visits).
- Need strict data isolation and KMS integration for PHI-sensitive routing in select environments.
- Ops team needs per-request audit logs and query-level retention controls for upcoming audits.

Goals you called out
- Sub-200ms tail latency for 512-token interactive queries (reporting UI).
- Consistent cost predictability for monthly forecast (we'll target a 20% reduction vs current baseline via batching/caching).
- Secure private deployment option for regulated datasets (VPC + customer-managed KMS).

Decision criteria (what you said matters most)
1) Latency & tail percentiles in production-like tests
2) Deterministic unit cost and straightforward autoscaling behavior
3) Security controls: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence readiness
4) Operational support for rollouts and runbooks

Open questions we captured
- Are there specific throughput SLOs for batch exports (nightly inference jobs)? (Todd)
- Curious about which fields in your clinical payload must be redacted before sending to hosted endpoints. (Security)
- Any vendor-level compliance evidence you want in advance of a bakeoff (SOC2 Type II, penetration test reports)?

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood will send a focused bakeoff test plan (3 scenarios: interactive 512-token UI, 2k-token summarization, nightly batch export) + dataset sampling guidance. [Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-test-plan-v1.docx]
2) We’ll run a 72-hour smoke run against a dedicated pool we provision for you (isolated tenant) — target start: week of 12/14.
3) Share SOC2 artifacts and checklist by EOD Wednesday.
4) Align on a simple cost baseline (redwood will run a quick cost parity calc once we have sample QPS).

Please confirm the bakeoff windows and the three test scenarios above. If you want different prioritization, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Attachments: symp-initial-qa.xlsx (your answers from the call), redwood-bakeoff-test-plan-v1.docx (proposed tests), redwood-tdr-deck.pdf (high-level tech + ops runbook)

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Neha — this looks great, thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Nightly batch exports: target throughput is ~1.2M tokens per hour during the 2–3 hour window. That should be part of the batch scenario.
- PHI redaction: we'll redact free-text clinical notes on our side for hosted tests; for private deployment we can send full payloads behind VPC.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II and our internal pen test report are sufficient for procurement to proceed. If you can surface the SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide that would help.

We’re good with the three scenarios; week of 12/14 works for an initial smoke run. Can you confirm expected RM (redwood-managed) vs PM (private-managed) options for the dedicated pool during the bakeoff?

Also, tagging procurement: Todd — can you confirm any PO or NDA prerequisites on your side?

—Jenna
Jenna Smith

Internal notes / quick vendor-context for the bakeoff: 

Competitive landscape (what I recommend we emphasize in the 72-hour runs)
- Vendor A (large public cloud endpoint): performs well on short-context interactive queries but struggles with consistent tail latency when KV cache hits are low. Cost model is opaque for reserved throughput.
- Vendor B (open-source hoster): cheaper on token cost but requires manual sharding to hit lower latency targets at scale — ops overhead high.
- Our angle: demonstrate consistent tail latency (p50/p95/p99) across session models with prefix caching + adaptive batching; show simple quantization profile to reduce unit cost without quality regression.

Suggested bakeoff tests (concrete)
1) Interactive UI simulation — 10k concurrent sessions, 512-token median context, measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
2) Long-context summarization — 2k-token end-to-end summary flow with KV-cache warmup and cold-start runs; compare latency and perplexity metrics.
3) Nightly batch export — bulk throughput test (1.2M tokens/hr target) with autoscale triggers and fallback to lower-cost variant if latency SLOs hit.

Metrics to capture (required for decision makers)
- p50/p95/p99 latency per scenario
- tokens/sec and total tokens processed
- cost per 1k tokens (normalized)
- error/retry rates and KV cache hit ratio

Open items for engineering before the run
- Need sample payload (anonymized) and a small validation harness from Symphony.
- We'll prepare a short runbook for the dedicated pool (start/stop, scaling knobs, fallbacks). [I’ll draft by 12/3]

I’ll also prepare a competitor-ops checklist that maps each test to what the other vendors typically miss (e.g., cold-start tail behavior).

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Confirmation if procurement requires an NDA before we provision the dedicated pool.

Proposed bakeoff schedule
- 12/14: provision pool and smoke run (team sync)

- 12/18: readout and decision calibration (internal + Symphony stakeholders)

Please review the attached test plan and the three scenarios. If that schedule looks good, I’ll send calendar invites and a short intake form for the payload.
